title: Armamentarium Turcico-Diabolicum (Olaus Fielkius Crone)
shelf_note: A Danish author's Latin occasional poem against the Turks, dedicated to the Duke of Württemberg. It has no tradition and no collection. Its only esoteric touch is the 'conjunctio ... septem Planetarum' omen on p.4. It is in period, but no shelf claims it.
structure_note: 18 records, 18 with OCR, 16 translated. No printed page numbers; signatures A2 and A3 on pp.3 and 5 run in order. Nothing stands out.

tr_errors.source: pia lumina, cuncti / Intendêre Polo

book_verdict: The OCR of a clean Latin print is very good. The translation is serviceable, with a few construction errors: 'fates' for 'crops', the Discord line, and 'Jove' for Jehovah. The centring arrows (->J.J.J.<-) show in the reader text.

title: 御定佩文韻府·卷二十三之七 (vol 411)
shelf_note: The Peiwenyunfu rhyme dictionary, filed in the generic 'universallibrary' collection. It is a reference work, not a primary source of any tradition the library curates.
structure_note: Only 12 of 123 records carry a printed number, with 5 backsteps and 5 repeats. These are most likely misread folio numerals in the fore-edge (p.95 '四十六', p.97 '四十七' run correctly), not a real disorder. 122 of 123 pages have OCR and 120 are translated.

book_verdict: The OCR of a dense, low-resolution woodblock page is mostly right, character by character. title: The answer of the Lord (Joanna Southcott, London 1813)
shelf_note: Southcott's millenarian prophecy, from the BPH. It sits well among the library's prophetic and esoteric material.
structure_note: From p.40 the images are two-page openings (printed 48|49 and 50|51), while p.39 is a single page (47). The scan alternates single pages and spreads, and the OCR treats each spread as two columns. The single printed backstep or repeat probably comes from these spread records. 107 of 107 pages have OCR and are translated: an English source run through a 'translation' that mostly echoes it and adds notes.

title: Aristophanes, Plutus and Clouds (with Scholia)
shelf_note: A 15th-century Greek manuscript of Aristophanes with scholia and interlinear glosses (Bodleian stamp). It is a valuable classical manuscript but belongs to no esoteric tradition, and no tradition or collection is set.
structure_note: Foliation (11 on p.29, 12 on p.31) runs correctly; the many backsteps and repeats (24 and 21 of 146) probably come from versos and recto foliation being read as page numbers, not from disorder. pages_translated is 308 in the count but 268 in the field: a counter drift.

title: 西陽雜俎·卷十六~卷二十 (vol 6)
shelf_note: Duan Chengshi's Youyang zazu (Siku quanshu manuscript copy), filed in the generic 'universallibrary'. The dream-divination entries touch on mantic lore, but no shelf is set.
structure_note: The title claims 卷十六~卷二十, but p.84 holds dream-divination entries (卷八 content), p.85 is the closing title '酉陽雜俎卷八', and p.86 is the Siku collators' roster ending a juan. Either the volume holds juan 8 or the catalogue range is wrong (class I7). The title also has 西 for 酉. Worth checking.
